title: Locality and residue fields of a directed local-ring colimit
statement: Let $I$ be a nonempty small directed poset and $(A_i,u_{ij})_{i\le j}$ a direct system of commutative local rings, where local means having a unique maximal ideal $\mathfrak m_i$. Suppose $u_{ij}^{-1}(\mathfrak m_j)=\mathfrak m_i$ for every $i\le j$. Let $(A,(\alpha_i))$ be its colimit in commutative rings [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. Then $M:=\bigcup_i\alpha_i(\mathfrak m_i)$ is the unique maximal ideal of $A$, and $\alpha_i^{-1}(M)=\mathfrak m_i$ for every $i$; in particular $A$ and all $\alpha_i$ are local. Write $k_i=A_i/\mathfrak m_i$ and $k=A/M$. The transition maps $[x]\mapsto[u_{ij}(x)]$ on the $k_i$ and the maps $\rho_i:k_i\to k$, $[x]\mapsto[\alpha_i(x)]$, are well-defined field homomorphisms. Each $\rho_i$ is injective, and $(k,(\rho_i))$ is a colimit of the residue-field diagram in commutative rings. No injectivity, surjectivity, flatness or finiteness assumption on the $u_{ij}$ is imposed.

source.place: Tag 04GI, lemma-colimit-henselian, proof: omitted argument that the ring colimit is local and its residue field is the colimit of the stage residue fields.

proof.text: The nonempty directed poset is filtered. Use the concrete filtered-colimit representation and eventual-equality theorems in [lem-pc-filtered-colimit-commrings-elementwise]. For a stage element x whose image is a unit, represent an inverse at another stage and move both to a common stage k. Their product maps to 1, so eventual equality makes that product equal to 1 at a later stage. Thus the image of x there is a unit. Reflect units along the two local transition maps to conclude that x is a unit. Every cocone leg is therefore local.

source.place: Tag 04GI, lemma-colimit-henselian, proof: expansion of the omitted locality and residue-field colimit argument; elementary ideal and quotient-ring calculations.

proof.text: The colimit is nonzero: otherwise 0 at any stage would have unit image and hence be a unit, contradicting that stage being local. Represent any colimit element x at a stage. At that local stage either its representative or 1 minus the representative is a unit; mapping this alternative to the colimit proves locality. By the local-unit criterion [lem-weil-pbc-local-ring-unit-criterion], or equivalently the definition of the maximal ideal as nonunits, every local cocone leg contracts the maximal ideal to the stage maximal ideal. Element representation now proves that the colimit maximal ideal equals the union of their images.

source.place: Tag 04GI, lemma-colimit-henselian, proof: expansion of the omitted locality and residue-field colimit argument; elementary ideal and quotient-ring calculations.

proof.text: Use Mathlib maximalIdeal_comap for the contraction formula. The canonical maps on residue fields exist for local maps and commute with the quotient maps. Each is injective because it is a unital ring homomorphism from a field to the nonzero residue field of the colimit.

source.place: Tag 04GI, lemma-colimit-henselian, proof: expansion of the omitted locality and residue-field colimit argument; elementary ideal and quotient-ring calculations.

proof.text: For any commutative ring B, compose the compatible maps from the stage residue fields with the stage quotient maps. Their compatibility gives a cocone on the original diagram. The colimit universal property [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit] gives t from the original colimit to B. If z lies in its maximal ideal, choose a representative x at a stage; contraction shows that x is in the stage maximal ideal, so t(z)=0. Factor t through the quotient by the maximal ideal with Ideal.Quotient.lift. Surjectivity of each stage quotient proves the required residue-map composites.

source.place: Tag 04GI, lemma-colimit-henselian, proof: expansion of the omitted locality and residue-field colimit argument; elementary ideal and quotient-ring calculations.

proof.text: For uniqueness, represent an arbitrary residue class by an element of the colimit, and that element by a stage element. The asserted composite of any candidate map with that stage residue map determines its value on the class, so it agrees with the constructed map. This works for arbitrary B, including the zero ring.

lean.statement: theorem local_colimit_residue_field {I : Type u} [PartialOrder I] [Nonempty I] [IsDirected I (· ≤ ·)] (F : I ⥤ CommRingCat.{u}) [∀ i : I, IsLocalRing (F.obj i)] [∀ (i j : I) (f : i ⟶ j), IsLocalHom (F.map f).hom] (c : Cocone F) (hc : IsColimit c) : ∃ (_ : IsLocalRing c.pt) (_ : ∀ i : I, IsLocalHom (c.ι.app i).hom), (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal c.pt : Set c.pt) = ⋃ i : I, (c.ι.app i).hom '' (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal (F.obj i) : Set (F.obj i)) ∧ (∀ i : I, (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal c.pt).comap (c.ι.app i).hom = IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal (F.obj i)) ∧ (∀ i : I, Function.Injective (IsLocalRing.ResidueField.map (R := F.obj i) (S := c.pt) (c.ι.app i).hom)) ∧ (∀ (B : CommRingCat.{u}) (h : ∀ i : I, IsLocalRing.ResidueField (F.obj i) →+* B), (∀ (i j : I) (f : i ⟶ j), (h j).comp (IsLocalRing.ResidueField.map (F.map f).hom) = h i) → ∃! g : IsLocalRing.ResidueField c.pt →+* B, ∀ i : I, g.comp (IsLocalRing.ResidueField.map (R := F.obj i) (S := c.pt) (c.ι.app i).hom) = h i)
